all_words.explanation: A sonnet is built on a fixed rhyme scheme, so rhyme is one of its defining features.
A glacier is a slow-moving mass of ice and has no connection with poetic form.
A sonnet is organised into stanzas, such as the octave and sestet, so the two words belong to the same discussion of poetic structure.
A harpoon is a fishing or whaling weapon and is unrelated to poetry or literary forms.
'Iambic pentameter' is the standard metre of the English sonnet, so the two words are regularly used together.
A saucer is a small dish for a cup and has no link to literary form or verse.

explanation: rhyme, stanza and iambic relate to the structure of the sonnet, while glacier, harpoon and saucer have nothing to do with poetic form.
